title: POC weekly — app invoke & SDK instrumentation review
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on SDK integration for app invoke patterns, function-calling edge cases, and telemetry gaps. Agreed to run targeted latency/cost benchmarks and produce a short security checklist for VectorHealth compliance team.
topics: SDK invocation patterns and retry behavior
Function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs
Telemetry/trace correlation and KV cache impacts
action_items: Anil Kapoor | Run 3-run latency+throughput benchmark on staging with 1/2/4 batch sizes and send results | 2026-01-22
Maya Chen | Share sample payloads and failure repros for structured output edge cases | 2026-01-18
Sophie Martinez | Send security summary (SOC2 snippets + network architecture notes) and Redwood security pack link | 2026-01-19
next_steps: Redwood to run bench and share spreadsheet
Customer to provide failing payload examples and acceptance criteria
Schedule a focused 30-min SE-only session on 2026-01-20 to debug a serializer issue
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We are at 14:00, I think we have 45 minutes on the calendar, cool. quick round robin?
[00:12] Maya Chen: Hi, Maya here. we ran another run this morning against staging, saw more of the malformed JSON when we hit retries.
[00:20] Derrick Alvarez: Derrick, product. we also noted some latency spikes when the app tried to do function calling in parallel.
[00:27] Anil Kapoor: Anil (Redwood SE) here. good to hear — we'll dig into the parallel invoke flow. first question, is the customer still using the JS SDK or the direct REST path?
[00:36] Maya Chen: JS SDK, yes. 0.9.3 pinned. we added a wrapper for retries.
[00:44] Tom Erickson: Tom from SRE. we're simulating 80 rps for a specific endpoint, that's where the structured output failures surface.
[00:52] Sophie Martinez: ok, thanks. quick agenda — SDK invocation quirks, function-calling structured output mismatches, and telemetry / kv-cache observations. anything else?
[01:03] Priya Nair: Security questions about audit logs and KMS — want to confirm where tokens are stored in the private deploy.
[01:11] Sophie Martinez: noted, we'll cover high level and I'll follow up with docs.
[01:16] Anil Kapoor: Maya, can you describe the failure mode again? is it truncated JSON, extra commas, or schema mismatch?
[01:25] Maya Chen: It's a couple things — mostly truncated responses when retry kicks in. sometimes the function call returns valid JSON, other times we get partial arrays and the client hangs. we also saw odd key names — like "resonse" spelled wrong in a couple outputs, not sure where that comes from, maybe transcription of the model?
[01:44] Derrick Alvarez: to add, when we parallelized two calls the second call would occasionally get an earlier call's response — looks like a client-level concurrency bug or kv-cache reuse issue.
[01:57] Anil Kapoor: ok that sounds like a race in the SDK's handling of streaming tokens + KV cache reuse. there are two places to investigate: the SDK's stream parser and the runtime's prefix cache.
[02:10] Sophie Martinez: quick note — are you on hosted Redwood or a private VPC deployment?
[02:16] Maya Chen: Hosted for now. evaluating private for PHI later, but the POC is hosted.
[02:22] Sophie Martinez: makes sense. hosted will have the same streaming semantics but we'll need to plan for VPC keys and KMS if you go private.
[02:30] Anil Kapoor: on the SDK side we introduced a patch last quarter to guard stream buffers per-request, but older SDKs pre-0.9.5 might still have a bug. what version did you say?
[02:41] Maya Chen: 0.9.3. we pinned because of a dependency issue with our bundler.
[02:46] Anil Kapoor: ok that's likely the culprit. two immediate mitigations: upgrade to 0.9.6 which has stream boundary fixes, or scope retries to non-streaming paths.
[02:56] Maya Chen: upgrading might be tricky but we'll try in a canary.
[03:00] Sophie Martinez: Anil, can you create a repro test for 0.9.3 -> 0.9.6 diff and share steps?
[03:07] Anil Kapoor: yes i'll run a quick harness. i'll also instrument the SDK to log a per-request id so we can see cross-talk.
[03:13] Tom Erickson: that per-request id will help SRE correlate traces. we currently send traces to honeycomb but need the request id in the trace context.
[03:22] Priya Nair: on security — will upgrading affect token storage? we have strict rotation policies.
[03:28] Sophie Martinez: upgrade won't change token storage. for hosted we use ephemeral tokens in transit, and we support customer-managed KMS for private. i'll email the security pack with specifics.
[03:37] Maya Chen: thanks. back to structured outputs — our schema expects a top-level "actions" array with objects {name, args}. the model sometimes emits a single object when it should be an array.
[03:52] Derrick Alvarez: and when retries happen it occasionally concatenates two JSON documents end-to-end, which the client fails to parse.
[04:02] Anil Kapoor: two possible fixes: 1) server-side envelope where we always wrap single objects in array before streaming; 2) client-side tolerant parser that accepts both forms. we prefer 1 for determinism, but it requires agreement on the contract.
[04:17] Maya Chen: we prefer server-side since multiple teams consume the response. Can Redwood add an optional 'force-array' flag on the model response?
[04:26] Anil Kapoor: we can add a response wrapper in the router for the POC deployment, yes. we will need to evaluate perf impact for large payloads.
[04:36] Sophie Martinez: note: this is a POC-only patch. if it works we can bake into release with tests.
[04:41] Tom Erickson: perf is important — we saw tokenization cost jump when we forced extra envelope. what's the expected size delta?
[04:49] Anil Kapoor: marginal for small objects; for big arrays we can stream elements without full materialization. it's more about CPU than token count in that case.
[04:58] Maya Chen: another oddity — function-calling spec: we use named tools, some tools accept binary blobs. when we run against the staging tool connector, we got a base64 decoding error.
[05:12] Anil Kapoor: can you paste the failing tool response after the call?
[05:16] Maya Chen: yes i'll attach in the ticket. it's intermittent.
[05:19] Derrick Alvarez: this ties back to parallelism — two tool calls on same session might share a buffer in our adapter.
[05:27] Anil Kapoor: i'll check the tool adapter logs. also, are you using function-calling via the SDK helper or custom envelope?
[05:34] Maya Chen: custom envelope. we used the helper initially but replaced it because of our serialization needs.
[05:40] Anil Kapoor: ok custom code increases surface area. recommend we repro using the SDK helper to isolate whether the runtime or the adapter is at fault.
[05:49] Sophie Martinez: next topic telemetry: you mentioned missing correlation between SDK traces and Honeycomb. can you describe your current headers?
[05:58] Tom Erickson: we add x-request-id and traceparent currently, but the SDK sometimes emits its own request id and doesn't forward traceparent on retries. so spans are split.
[06:10] Anil Kapoor: we recently released a header-foward patch for retries; older SDK clients lose tracecontext on request restart. this is similar to the stream bug — upgrade or patch the wrapper.
[06:22] Priya Nair: for compliance we'll need audit logs of every function/tool invocation and user ID mapping. does Redwood provide an export?
[06:31] Sophie Martinez: yes hosted includes an audit events feed; for private we can enable streaming to your SIEM. i'll include the audit log schema in the pack.
[06:39] Maya Chen: perfect. one more thing — cost. when we turned on per-request caching for prefixes, we saw cost fall by 18% but latency bumped 30ms in p95.
[06:51] Derrick Alvarez: so tradeoff question: do we prefer lower cost or lower latency? for customer-facing features latency matters more.
[06:59] Anil Kapoor: you can tune cache TTL and batch sizes. Redwood Optimize (we sometimes call it Redwood Optimise in docs) has a suggestion engine that recommends config for throughput vs cost. we'll run it on your traces.
[07:11] Maya Chen: can you run optimize on the staging traces? we can share a sanitized trace export.
[07:15] Anil Kapoor: yes send the sanitized traces, we'll run offline analysis and return a recommended profile.
[07:21] Sophie Martinez: circling back to action items — Anil will run benchmarks with explicit batch sizes and stream vs non-streaming; Maya will send failing payloads; Sophie will send security pack. any blockers for that?
[07:32] Maya Chen: none. Derek — sorry Derrick — we'll prioritize the failing payloads.
[07:36] Derrick Alvarez: yes we'll collect and upload by Monday.
[07:40] Tom Erickson: can we have a short SE-only session to reproduce the serializer concat issue?
[07:44] Sophie Martinez: yes proposed 2026-01-20 10:00am PT. we'll set a separate invite.
[07:50] Priya Nair: quick compliance Q: do you maintain a public data residency map for hosted regions? we need EU-only for some data sets.
[07:58] Sophie Martinez: yes eu-west and eu-central are available; i'll include region notes in the security pack.
[08:06] Maya Chen: thanks. a small nit on function-calling: we saw the helper's schema include 'metadata' property which our parser treats as reserved word. any way to rename?
[08:16] Anil Kapoor: we can namespace tool-metadata under _meta to reduce collisions; again a POC-level adapter.
[08:22] Maya Chen: that would help.
[08:24] Sophie Martinez: ok last 5 minutes, let's recap and next steps.
[08:29] Anil Kapoor: recap from SE: repro harness for SDK 0.9.3->0.9.6, instrument per-request ids, inspect tool-adapter for base64 error, run batch/latency bench.
[08:42] Maya Chen: to-do from customer: upload failing payloads, try canary upgrade to 0.9.6 on a small host.
[08:50] Sophie Martinez: Redwood to send security pack and schedule SE-only on 2026-01-20 10:00am PT.
[08:57] Derrick Alvarez: we'll also define acceptance criteria for structured output: must be an array or wrapped and pass our schema validator 100% of the time in canary for 24 hours.
[09:10] Sophie Martinez: great, i'll capture those in the ticket. anything else?
[09:14] Tom Erickson: small ask — include sample curl to reproduce streaming boundary test.
[09:19] Anil Kapoor: will do, will include in the bench doc.
[09:23] Sophie Martinez: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the notes and links. meeting adjourned.
[09:30] *call ended*

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-attributions (Speaker labels sometimes show internal names) and typical speech disfluencies. references: "security pack" link will be shared by email; bench spreadsheet to be uploaded to the shared POC drive.
